text: Nearly every real ServiceNow integration fits one of three pattern categories: inbound, outbound, or event-driven and bidirectional. Knowing which one you need is the first real decision in building any integration.

Inbound means an external system pushes data into ServiceNow. A Scripted REST API, from course six, is a custom endpoint an external system calls with an HTTP POST — the right fit when the data needs to land in near real time. Import Sets, from course two, take in batch data, like a nightly CSV export, through staging tables and a Transform Map — the right fit when the external system can't call an API directly, or the data simply arrives as a batch.

Outbound is the mirror image: ServiceNow initiates the call. A REST Message is a reusable definition of an HTTP endpoint — URL, headers, authentication, and named methods — that a Business Rule, Script Include, or Flow can invoke whenever ServiceNow's own process needs to reach outside itself.

IntegrationHub, starting in Chapter five, builds on the same idea at a higher level. A spoke packages one or more REST Messages behind a reusable, drag-and-drop action a Flow can call — it doesn't replace REST Messages, it wraps them for easier reuse.

Event-driven integration is built around something happening — an event — that immediately produces a notification pushed to whoever's listening, rather than either side repeatedly asking if anything changed. Many production integrations end up bidirectional in practice: two separate, simpler patterns running side by side, not one mechanism doing two things.

Three questions settle almost every pattern choice: who initiates the data movement, how real-time it needs to be, and whether the external system can even make outbound HTTP calls at all. That last constraint is exactly when an old-fashioned batch Import Set is still the right answer today.

Inbound, outbound, event-driven — three shapes, chosen by who initiates and how fast it needs to move. Next up: the protocols underneath these patterns — REST, SOAP, and event-driven messaging compared directly.
